# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the enrichment/categorization stage.

# Transaction Enrichment / Categorization — Repository Map

## 0. Headline finding first

**Items 3 and 4 of your request do not exist in this repository.**

- There are **zero** test fixtures, labelled corpora, JSON/CSV/YAML data files, or expected-output files.
- There is **no** test harness, no baseline/golden-file diffing, no `pytest`/`unittest` code, no `conftest.py`, no CI config, no `Makefile`, no `README`.
- The repo contains exactly **54 tracked files**: 52 `.py` files + `Dockerfile` + `.gitignore`. Verified via `git ls-files` and a full `find`.
- Single commit history (`047782b import codebase`), one branch (`main`), no stashes, no deleted files in history (`git log --all --diff-filter=D` is empty), 60 total git objects.
- `.gitignore` line 47 contains `*.csv` — so any labelled CSV corpora that the original team used were deliberately excluded from version control and are not recoverable from this repo.

Everything else below (items 1 and 2) is present and extensive. I also verified the pipeline is runnable in-process and produced a working smoke test (Section 6).

---

## 1. Repository layout

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                                     # gunicorn categorizationapp:app on :9898
├── .gitignore                                     # NOTE line 47: *.csv  (fixtures excluded)
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                                   # pkg deps, lines 7-19
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                            # Flask app object + logger (31 lines)
        ├── Controller.py                          # HTTP routes / pipeline orchestration (936 lines)
        ├── BankScripts/                           # 35 per-bank category+counterparty modules
        └── UtilityScripts/                        # 13 shared modules (regex banks, purpose, cleanup)
```

Total ~11,145 lines of Python. Largest files:

| Lines | File |
|---|---|
| 1971 | `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` |
| 936 | `Controller.py` |

---

## 2. Pipeline architecture (entry point → stages)

**Entry point:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`

| Line | Route / function |
|---|---|
| `Controller.py:51-53` | `home()` — `GET /` health check |
| `Controller.py:55-67` | `recurrentTransactions()` — `POST /recurrentTransactions` |
| `Controller.py:69-936` | `categorizeTransaction()` — `POST /categorizeTransaction` (the main enrichment endpoint) |

Request payload keys read at `Controller.py:74-81`: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`.

`Controller.py:91-932` is a giant `if/elif` on `bank` — **the identical 6-stage block is copy-pasted 35 times**, once per bank. Canonical instance is `Controller.py:91-114` (ANDHRA_BANK):

```
1. AppUtil.clean_input_df(transactions)                    Controller.py:87
2. categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)  → transactionCategory + partyName   (stage 1)
3. card_clean_names() + card_purpose()                     only if accountType == "CREDIT_CARD"
4. purpose(transactions, accountType)                      → transactionSubcategory + merchantType (stage 2)
5. clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)            → canonicalise partyName                (stage 3)
6. internal_payment(...)   if accountHolder non-empty
7. salary_detection(...)   if accountType == "SAVING"
8. pfm_categorization() + simple_description()  if isPFMEnabled
```

Response serialised at `Controller.py:934-936` (`to_json(orient='records')`).

### Enriched output columns produced
`transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`, `party2` (space-stripped partyName used as a secondary match key), `internalName`, `isInternalPayment`, `Group_ID`, `pfmCategoryOne`, `pfmCategoryTwo`, `pfmCategoryType`, `pfmSimpleDescription`.

### Required input columns
`description` (6,109 references), `type` (1,333), `amount` (141), `remark` (42 — cheque numbers), `balanceAfterTransaction` (1), `transactionDate` (used by `SalaryDetection.py:56`).

---

## 3. ITEM 1 — Code that derives a transaction "category" from narration/reference text

### 3.1 The 35 per-bank category classifiers (`BankScripts/`)

### 3.2 NEFT / IMPS / UPI / RTGS rail detection

Detected purely by narration prefix regex inside each bank's rule list. HDFC examples:

| Line | Rule |
|---|---|
| `HDFC.py:57` | `"-TPT-"` → `TPT` |
| `HDFC.py:58` | `"^UPI\|UPI-?\s?"` → `UPI` |
| `HDFC.py:59` | `"IMPS-"` → `IMPS` |
| `HDFC.py:60` | `"NEFT [CcDd][Rr]-\|[0-9]NEFT TO\|^BULK NEFT"` → `NEFT` |
| `HDFC.py:61` | `"RTGS"` → `RTGS` |
| `HDFC.py:62` | `"^APBS"` → `AADHAAR_PAY` |
| `HDFC.py:63` | `"\bIB\b FUNDS"` → `INTERNET_BANKING` |
| `HDFC.py:22` | `"REV-UPI\|UPI RET-"` → `UPI_REVERSAL` |
| `HDFC.py:23` | `"REV-IMPS"` → `IMPS_REVERSAL` |
| `HDFC.py:28` | `"NEFT RETURN"` → `NEFT_RETURN` |
| `HDFC.py:29` | `"RTGS-RETURN"` → `RTGS_RETURN` |
| `HDFC.py:34` | `"^\.IMPS"` → `IMPS_CHARGES` |

SBI's rail regexes live in `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py:43-62` (`SBI_INB_1..8`, `SBI_IMPS_1..3`); Kotak's in `BankRegexConstants.py:195-218` (`IMPS_PATTERN1..8`, `NEFT_PATTERN0..7`, `KT_RTGS_PATTERN`, `RTGS_PATTERN1`); Union Bank's in `BankRegexConstants.py:120-129` (`UB_NEFT_1..8_UNION`, `UB_RTGS_1..2_UNION`).

### 3.3 Cheque detection

Cheque categories: `CHEQUE_PAID`, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `CHEQUE_RETURN`, `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY`, `CHEQUE_RETURN_CHARGES`, `CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL`, `CHEQUE_BOUNCE`, `STOP_CHEQUE_CHARGES`, `INWARD_CHEQUE_RETURN`, `OUTWARD_CHEQUE_RETURN`.

Two detection mechanisms:

**(a) narration regex** — e.g. `HDFC.py:69-75`, `SBI.py:21-47`, `StandardCharted.py:43-45`, `Syndicate.py:52-57`, `UnionBank.py:50-51`, `Saraswat.py:38-39`, `UCO.py:37-38`.

**(b) `remark` field looking like a cheque number** — a distinct heuristic:

| Line | Rule |
|---|---|
| `YES.py:52-53` | `remark` matches `^[0-9]{3,6}$` → DEBIT=`CHEQUE_PAID`, CREDIT=`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` |
| `UCO.py:44-45` | same `^[0-9]{3,6}$` |
| `RBL.py:49-50` | `^[0-9]{1,3}$` |
| `PNB.py:60-61` | `^[0-9]{5}$` / `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| `SouthIndian.py:32` | `[0-9]{6}` |
| `TamilnadMerchantile.py:33-34` | `^[0-9]{5,}/` |
| `HDFC.py:100` | `remark.str.len()==16` and `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` |

**(c) cheque-return reason classification** — `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:145-147` maps the return reason text into `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` vs `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE`, using `RegexConstants.py:86` (`TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, ~55 alternatives incl. `Refer to drawer`, `SIGNATURE MISMAT`, `POST DATED`) and `RegexConstants.py:87` (`INSUFF_BOUNCE`). Line `Purpose.py:146` re-runs the match on a whitespace-stripped copy of the description to catch run-together bank text.

Cheque-specific counterparty regexes: `BankRegexConstants.py:81-90` (`HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10`), `:140-148` (`PNB_CHQ_0..8`), `:314-318` (`CHQ_PATTERN1..4`, `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK`), `:361-362` (`CHQ_CLEAN`, `CHQ_CLEAN2`), `:380-383` (`UCO_CHQ_PATTERN1..4`), `:263-297` (`FT_CHQ_PATTERN1..37`), `:432` (`CHQ_CLEAN_SCB`).

### 3.4 Account verification / penny-drop detection

This is a well-defined "₹1 probe" detector. Pattern is always *narration regex* **AND** *amount ∈ {1, -1}*. All 29 sites:

| File:line | Regex source | Amount guard |
|---|---|---|
| `Andhra.py:12` | `ACC_VERI_ANDHRA` (`BankRegexConstants.py:365`) | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `AuSmallFinanceBank.py:12` | inline `"Acc validation\|AC VALIDATION\|A/ C VALIDATION"` | `eq(1)` |
| `Axis.py:24` | `BANK_VER` (`BankRegexConstants.py:327`) | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `Axis.py:25` | inline `"MANDATE\|Mandate"` | `eq(1)` |
| `Axis.py:26` | *(no narration)* any CREDIT | `eq(1)` |
| `BOB.py:12` | inline `"verif\|nydrop\|valida\|GOOGLE.*TEMPOR\|Accountv\|bankAccountV\|Authenticat\|detailsv?\|ntvalid\|BeneficiaryV\|TowardsBeneA"` | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `BOI.py:12` | `BANK_VER_BOI` (`BankRegexConstants.py:110`) | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `BankOfMaharashtra.py:36` | `BANK_VER` | `isin(["1","-1"])` ⚠ string compare |
| `BankOfMaharashtra.py:37` | *(no narration)* any CREDIT | `isin(["1"])` ⚠ |
| `Canara.py:19` | `BANK_VERIF` (`BankRegexConstants.py:321`) | `lt(1)` ⚠ excludes exactly 1 |
| `Central.py:12` | `ACC_VERI_CB` (`BankRegexConstants.py:415`) | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `HDFC.py:13` | `BANK_VER` | `lt(2)` |
| `ICICI.py:11` | `BANK_VER_ICICI` (`BankRegexConstants.py:69`) | `isin([1,-1])` AND NOT `\bRVSL\b` |
| `IDBI.py:12` | inline (extended list w/ `AccVer\|PennyD\|bankAc\|Accoun`) | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `IDFC.py:12` | inline (same extended list) | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `Indusind.py:29` | `BANK_VER` | `isin(["1","-1"])` ⚠ |
| `Indusind.py:30` | inline `"MANDATE\|Mandate"` | `eq(1)` |
| `Indusind.py:31` | *(no narration)* any DEBIT | `isin(["1"])` ⚠ |
| `Karnataka.py:12` | inline | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `Kotak.py:13` | inline `"Karz Xx4002"` | `eq(1)` + CREDIT |
| `Kotak.py:14` | inline `"^Received from [A-Z]"` | `eq(1)` + CREDIT |
| `PNB.py:12` | `ACC_VERIFY_PNB` (`BankRegexConstants.py:133`) | `lt(2)` |
| `Paytm.py:15` | `ACC_VERIF_PAYTM` (`BankRegexConstants.py:428`) | *(no amount guard)* |
| `Paytm.py:16` | inline `"IMPS"` | `eq(1)` + CREDIT |
| `RBL.py:15` | `ACC_VERI_RBL` (`BankRegexConstants.py:410`) | `lt(2)` |
| `SBI.py:12` | `ACC_VERIF` (`BankRegexConstants.py:6`) | `eq(1)` + CREDIT |
| `SouthIndian.py:12` | inline `"Account Validation\|A/ C VALIDATION\|Acc validation\|/AccVer\b"` | `eq(1)` |
| `StandardCharted.py:13` | `ACC_VERI_SCB` (`BankRegexConstants.py:431`) | `eq(1)` |
| `Syndicate.py:12` | `ACC_VERI_SYNDICATE` (`BankRegexConstants.py:163`) | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `TamilnadMerchantile.py:13` | inline `"Accvalidation\|Accountvali"` | `eq(1)` |
| `UnionBank.py:12` | `ACC_VERI_UNION` (`BankRegexConstants.py:116`) | `isin([1,-1])` |
| `YES.py:14` | `ACC_VERI_YES` (`BankRegexConstants.py:396`) | `eq(1)` |

Downstream consumers of `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`:
- `Purpose.py:165` — a `LOAN` subcategory with amount ±1 is *reclassified* to `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.
- `Purpose.py:173` — blanks `transactionSubcategory` for anything matching `VERIFICATION`.
- `SalaryDetection.py:205-206` — blanks subcategory for `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` and any amount == 1.
- `Axis.py:123`, `ICICI.py:166-167`, `IDFC.py:71-72` — *suppress* counterparty extraction when category is `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.
- `Paytm.py:96` — blanks `partyName` for `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.
- `SimpleDescription.py:8` — in `transactionCategoryList`, so no partyName is prefixed.

Note: 14 banks (`BOB`, `IDBI`, `IDFC`, `Karnataka`, `AuSmallFinanceBank`, `SouthIndian`, `TamilnadMerchantile`) inline near-duplicate copies of the same verification regex rather than sharing a constant — a real duplication/drift hazard.

### 3.5 Stage 2 — subcategory / merchantType (`UtilityScripts/Purpose.py`)

`purpose(transactions, accountType)` at `Purpose.py:9`. Four sequential `np.select` blocks:

| Lines | Target column | Rule count |
|---|---|---|
| `Purpose.py:12-152` | `transactionSubcategory` | 136 rules (SALARY, LOAN, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, INVESTMENT, FUEL, TRAVEL, RENT, UTILITY_BILL, FOOD_*, E_COMMERCE, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, INTERNAL_PAYMENT, …) |
| `Purpose.py:154-170` | `transactionCategory` (override) | 12 rules (TDS, TAX_REFUND, CASHBACK, REFUND, DIRECT_TAX, INDIRECT_TAX, TAX, FIXED_DEPOSIT, INTEREST, **ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION** at :165) |
| `Purpose.py:172-178` | blank subcategory for charge/reversal cats | 2 rules |
| `Purpose.py:182-278` | `merchantType` | 92 rules (NBFC, HFC, Instant Loan, Flight, Railways, Electricity, Gas, Water, Mutual Fund, Pharmacy, …) |
| `Purpose.py:280-291` | `transactionSubcategory` (merchantType feedback) | 7 rules |
| `Purpose.py:293-298` | blank merchantType for reversals | 1 rule |

Each rule matches against one of three fields: `transactions.description` (raw narration), `transactions.partyName` (extracted counterparty), or `transactions.party2` (space-stripped counterparty).

### 3.6 Credit-card path

- `UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py` — `card_purpose(transactions)` at :9. Writes `transactionSubcategory` (:65), `transactionCategory` (:72), `merchantType` (:146), `transactionSubcategory` again (:157). Matches only on `description` (cards have no separate party field yet).
- `UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py` — `card_clean_names(transactions)` at :9; single 900-rule `np.select` writing `partyName` at :926.

### 3.7 PFM roll-up

`UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` — `pfm_categorization(transactions)` at :8.
- `pfmCategoryOne` at :81 (from 64 rules, :14-78, default `UNCATEGORISED`)
- `pfmCategoryTwo` at :191 (from 104 rules, :83-188)
- `pfmCategoryType` at :204 (EXPENSE / INCOME / TRANSFER, lists at :193-195)
- `TRANSFER_PFM1` list at :12 folds `NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/UPI/CHEQUE_PAID/CHEQUE_DEPOSIT/TPT/CASH_DEPOSIT` into `TRANSFER`.

`UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` — `simple_description(transactions)` at :6, builds `pfmSimpleDescription = partyName + " - " + <TransactionCategory enum label>` (:12-17). **Bug worth noting:** `transactions.transactionCategory.get(0)` at :12 reads only row 0's category and applies its label to every row.

### 3.8 Category vocabularies (enums)

- `UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` — `class TransactionCategory(enum.Enum)` at :3, 171 lines. Cheque members at :9, :27, :44, :48, :57, :63, :101, :161, :163, :164, :168. `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION="Account Verification"` at **:83**.
- `UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` — `class TransactionSubcategory` , 135 lines (cheque members at :18, :36, :37, :63).

## 4. ITEM 2 — Code that extracts a "counterparty" / payee / sender name from raw narration

### 4.1 Primitive extraction helpers — `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`

These are the atomic building blocks used by every extraction rule in the codebase:

| Line | Function | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `AppUtil.py:6` | `clean_input_df(transactions)` | strip description, coerce `amount`/`balanceAfterTransaction` numeric |
| `AppUtil.py:14` | `sep_by_(description, n1, n2)` | split on `/`, join slice `[n1:n2]` |
| `AppUtil.py:17` | `sep_by_dash` | split on `-` |
| `AppUtil.py:20` | `sep_by_wave` | split on `~` |
| `AppUtil.py:23` | `sep_by_star` | split on `*` |

### 6.5 If you need to build the missing harness

The natural seam is the stage-2/3 boundary. A replay harness would:

1. Load a fixture of `{bank, acc_type, accountHolder, transactions[{description, remark, type, amount, balanceAfterTransaction, transactionDate}]}` plus expected `{transactionCategory, transactionSubcategory, merchantType, partyName}`.
2. Call `clean_input_df` → `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` → `purpose` → `clean_names` (optionally `internal_payment`, `salary_detection`, `pfm_categorization`, `simple_description`) — i.e. replicate `Controller.py:87-114` without Flask. The one Flask coupling is `app.logger` (`Purpose.py:1`, `CleanName.py:1`, `CardPurpose.py:1`, `CardCleanNames.py:1`) — importing `categorizationapp` satisfies it, as my smoke test shows.
3. Diff the four output columns against the baseline.

Gotchas that will bite a harness author:
- `np.select` is **first-match-wins**; inserting a rule anywhere changes downstream results, so any baseline is order-sensitive.
- `SalaryDetection.salary_detection` returns `None` on any exception and the caller silently discards the failure (`Controller.py:108-109`) — a harness must assert on this explicitly.
- `SalaryDetection.py:56` hard-codes `format="%d/%m/%Y"` for `transactionDate`.
- `BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37` and `Indusind.py:29-31` compare `amount` against the **strings** `"1"`/`"-1"`, so those verification rules never fire after `clean_input_df` coerces to numeric (`AppUtil.py:9`).
- `Canara.py:19` uses `amount.lt(1)`, excluding the exact ₹1 penny-drop it is meant to catch.
- `SimpleDescription.py:12` uses `.get(0)`, applying row 0's category label to all rows.
- `party2` is never dropped (`CleanName.py:1969` commented out) so it appears in API output; a baseline should either include it or filter it.

import sys, pandas as pd
sys.path.insert(0,'/app/categorizationapp')
import categorizationapp
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.AppUtil import clean_input_df
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.Purpose import purpose
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CleanName import clean_names
import importlib

def run(bank_mod, bank_fn, bank_name, rows, acct="SAVING"):
    m = importlib.import_module('categorizationapp.BankScripts.'+bank_mod)
    f = getattr(m, bank_fn)
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for c,d in [('remark',''),('type','DEBIT'),('amount',100.0),('balanceAfterTransaction',1000.0),('transactionDate','01/01/2022')]:
        if c not in df: df[c]=d
    df = df.fillna({'remark':''})
    t = clean_input_df(df)
    t = f(t, acct)
    t = purpose(t, acct)
    t = clean_names(t, acct, bank_name)
    pd.set_option('display.width',250); pd.set_option('display.max_colwidth',60)
    print(t[['description','remark','type','amount','transactionCategory','transactionSubcategory','partyName']].to_string())

 'YES':('YES','categorize_YES_transactions'),
}
EXTRA_HOLDER = {'BANK_OF_MAHARASHTRA','CITY_UNION','UCO'}

def enrich(bank, rows, acct="SAVING", holder=""):
    mod, fn = BANKS[bank]
    m = importlib.import_module('categorizationapp.BankScripts.'+mod)
    f = getattr(m, fn)
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows).copy()
    for c,d in [('remark',''),('type','DEBIT'),('amount',100.0),('balanceAfterTransaction',1000.0),('transactionDate','01/01/2022')]:
        if c not in df: df[c]=d
    df['remark']=df['remark'].fillna('')
    t = clean_input_df(df)
    t = f(t, acct, holder) if bank in EXTRA_HOLDER else f(t, acct)
    t = purpose(t, acct)
    t = clean_names(t, acct, bank)
    return t

def scan(rows, acct="SAVING", cols=('transactionCategory','partyName')):
    for b in BANKS:
        try:
            t = enrich(b, rows, acct)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"{b:24s} ERROR {e}"); continue
        out=[]
        for i in range(len(t)):
            out.append(" | ".join(str(t[c].iloc[i]) for c in cols))
        print(f"{b:24s} " + "  ||  ".join(out))

steps.message:
All five findings clear, with a verified-clean blast radius.

## Diagnosis

The regressed fixtures all belong to the **Canara** enrichment path (`BankScripts/Canara.py`). Four of the five were off-by-one field/threshold slips that stand out against the idiom used by every other bank module in the repo; one was a missing rule.

| # | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **F-1** | No rule keyed on a bare cheque number in the note field at all — such debits fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Every peer module (`YES.py:52`, `UCO.py:44`, `RBL`, `PNB`) carries a `^[0-9]{3,6}$` note rule; Canara had none. | Added the note rule (and the same-shaped bare-digit narration), **appended last** so any narration-based rule still wins — it can therefore only rescue rows that previously defaulted to `TRANSFER`. |
| **F-2** | `^CHQ PAID-` took dash segment **1**, which is the clearing tag on the three-part `CHQ PAID-<clearing tag>-<payee>` layout. The sibling rule for `Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` already correctly took segment 2. | Folded `MICR CLG`/`CTS`/inward/outward clearing tags into that existing clearing-tag rule. |
| **F-3** | `NEFT-` took dash segment **1** = the UTR. Because the ref is all digits, the downstream `^[0-9]{5,}` scrubber then wiped it — hence a *blank* name with a correct category. Every peer (`BOB:102`, `ICICI:152`, `IDBI:94`, `RBL:98`, `YES:108`) uses segment 2 for this shape. | Added a guarded rule taking segment 2 **only when segment 1 is a reference token**, so genuine `NEFT-<payee>` rows are untouched. |
| **F-4** | Same slip on the instant-payment rails: `UPI/[CD]R` and `-IMPS-[CD]R/` took field **2** (the 12-digit RRN) instead of field 3. `Bandhan:59` and `CityUnion:102` use field 3. Depending on whether the ref survived the scrubber, this surfaced either a bare RRN or a blank. | Added reference-guarded rules (`.../[0-9]+/`) ahead of the existing ones. |
| **F-5** | `amount.lt(1)` — a textbook off-by-one that **excludes the ₹1 penny drop** it exists to catch while accepting sub-rupee amounts. `HDFC:13`, `PNB:12`, `RBL:15` all use `lt(2)`. | `lt(1)` → `lt(2)`; strictly additive over the previous coverage. |

## Verification

I built a 5,712-row Canara probe corpus (≈200 narrations × both types × 6 amount/note combinations × both account types) and diffed all five derived fields against `HEAD`:

- **5,186 rows byte-identical**; 526 changed, and a programmatic assertion confirms **0 unexplained changes** — every category change is either a ₹1 verification credit or a bare-instrument-number cheque debit, and every name change goes from blank / a pure reference token / a clearing tag *to* a real name.
- **0 rows lost a name.** The first sweep did surface real collateral here: rows relabelled `CHEQUE_PAID` silently lost their payee, because ~9 payee rules are gated on `transactionCategory == "TRANSFER"`. I added a `transfer_like` mask so rows that are cheques *only* by virtue of the bare instrument number keep the transfer-style extraction they already had.
- Only `Canara.py` is touched; the other 34 bank modules are unchanged and all still import. Full pipeline verified end-to-end (purpose → clean names → internal payment → salary → PFM), where the restored names now also correct downstream PFM labels (`Swiggy` → `RESTAURANTS_DINING`, previously `UNCATEGORISED`).

Two notes for you:

1. **The repo contains no fixtures and no test harness** — no corpus, no baseline files, no test runner (`.gitignore` excludes `*.csv`, so the labelled corpora were never committed). I could not replay your actual fixtures, so I reconstructed each finding from the narration layouts implied by the code. F-2's quoted narration is what pinned the bank to Canara; the others I confirmed reproduce there. The probe corpus and diff harness are in `/tmp/opencode/` if you want to re-point them at the real corpus.
2. **Pre-existing, unrelated:** `POST /categorizeTransaction` returns HTTP 500 on multi-row payloads at `Controller.py:935` (`to_json` → `OverflowError`), because `SalaryDetection` writes a 2-D `cut_tree` result into `Group_ID`. I confirmed this fails identically at `HEAD` and left it alone as out of scope — but it will block anything that exercises the HTTP layer rather than the stage functions.
